concepts.why: The presence of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, a markedly dilated fetal bladder, oligohydramnios, and impaired renal function, along with postnatal findings of bladder wall irregularity and thickening, bilateral ureteral dilation, and urinary retention, are consistent with the diagnosis of Posterior Urethral Valves.

The combination of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, a markedly dilated fetal bladder, oligohydramnios, and impaired renal function, along with the presence of a left perirenal fluid collection, are features that can be seen in Prune Belly Syndrome.

The presence of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, a left perirenal fluid collection, and impaired renal function, along with the postnatal finding of mixed long and short T1 and T2 signals with internal light bands, are consistent with the diagnosis of Ureteropelvic Junction Obstruction.

The presence of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, a left perirenal fluid collection, and impaired renal function, along with the postnatal finding of mixed long and short T1 and T2 signals with internal light bands, are features that can be seen in Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney.

The presence of bilateral renal enlargement and hydronephrosis, impaired renal function, and postnatal findings of bladder wall irregularity and thickening, bilateral ureteral dilation, and urinary retention, are consistent with the diagnosis of Congenital Megacalycosis.
